newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO's Solana to visit Moscow in March. [CORRECTED 18:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NATO's Solana to visit Moscow in March. [CORRECTED 18:39 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects the headline and the text to make clear the visit is in March and not April.)

NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana will visit Moscow on March 8 and 9 for a new round of talks on a new deal with Russia ahead of the alliance's planned eastwards enlargement, alliance officials said on Friday.

The officials declined to give other details of the visit in which Solana will follow up two previous rounds of talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on a Russia-NATO charter or document.
The announcement of more talks follows an intensive bout of diplomacy in recent weeks.

On Friday, Solana was quoted as saying a binding text governing post-Cold War relations between the alliance and Moscow could be ready for signing by the time of a July summit in Madrid at which NATO will invite new members to join.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are the favourites with Slovenia and Romania making strong last-minute pushes.

Solana and Primakov met in Brussels last Sunday amid signs that Moscow, although still strongly opposed to enlargement, had concluded it could not prevent it and should try to cut a deal as quickly as possible.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin said he thought a compromise would be reached at a Helsinki summit with U.S. President Bill Clinton on March 20 and 21.
